# Gladys Assistant

> Gladys Assistant is a privacy-first, open-source, self-hosted home automation platform. It runs locally on your hardware (mini-PC, Raspberry Pi, NAS) with no mandatory cloud. Alternative to Home Assistant, focused on simplicity, local control, and European privacy standards.

## What is Gladys Assistant?

Gladys Assistant is free, open-source smart home software (Apache 2.0) created in 2013 by Pierre-Gilles Leymarie. It lets you control lights, sensors, cameras, and automations from a single local dashboard. Data stays on your machine — no tracking, no data resale. The current major version is Gladys Assistant 5 (released August 2026), with a redesigned, mobile-first interface.

## Quick facts

- **Price**: the software is free forever. The optional Gladys Plus subscription starts at $7.99/month in the US and Canada ($11.99 for the full plan), €6.99/month in Europe, with a 1-month free trial, no credit card required, cancel anytime.
- **Runs on**: any Linux machine with Docker (mini-PC, Raspberry Pi, Synology or other NAS, server). Setup is guided by step-by-step documentation; no YAML or configuration files.
- **Works offline**: devices, scenes and automations run on your local network and keep working when the internet is down.
- **Privacy**: self-hosted, no ads, no tracking, no data resale. Remote access through Gladys Plus is end-to-end encrypted.
- **AI and voice**: a natural-language AI assistant (chat, Telegram, voice assistant widget) powered by open-weight models hosted in France (Scaleway), included in Gladys Plus. Not run by Amazon, Google or OpenAI.
- **Support**: an active community forum, automatically translated so English and French speakers read and answer each other seamlessly, plus email support (hello@gladysassistant.com). Independent project: no investors, funded by Gladys Plus subscribers.
- **Available worldwide**: the software and Gladys Plus work in any country, with prices in USD in North America. The interface is available in English, French and German.

## Key pages

- [Homepage](https://gladysassistant.com/): Product overview and getting started
- [Documentation](https://gladysassistant.com/docs/): Installation guides (Docker, Raspberry Pi, mini-PC, Synology)
- [Integrations](https://gladysassistant.com/docs/integrations/): Zigbee2MQTT, Matter, MQTT, Shelly, Sonos, cameras, and more
- [MCP server](https://gladysassistant.com/docs/integrations/mcp/): Connect Claude Desktop, Perplexity, or Mistral to your smart home via Model Context Protocol
- [Agent authentication](https://gladysassistant.com/auth.md): How AI agents authenticate with Gladys via MCP API keys
- [AI control](https://gladysassistant.com/docs/integrations/openai/): Natural-language smart home control with open-weight LLMs hosted in France (Scaleway)
- [Gladys Plus](https://gladysassistant.com/plus/): Optional subscription — encrypted remote access, daily backups, voice assistants, AI, MCP over the internet
- [Open metrics](https://gladysassistant.com/open/): Public transparency data (active instances, community stats)
- [Voice assistant](https://gladysassistant.com/docs/dashboard/voice-assistant/): Talk to your home from the dashboard, a wall tablet or a phone

## Differentiators vs Home Assistant

- Simpler UI and lower learning curve for beginners
- Privacy-first by design: self-hosted, no mandatory cloud
- Native MCP server to connect AI agents (Claude, Perplexity, Mistral) to your home
- Open-weight AI models hosted in Europe (Scaleway, France) via Gladys Plus
- External integrations: community integrations packaged as Docker containers, published on GitHub and installable in one click, that anyone can create without a pull request or review, and that run in an isolated sandbox so they cannot destabilize the instance (installing one needs no command line, no YAML and no technical skills)
- Strong focus on Matter, Zigbee2MQTT, and open protocols

## Supported protocols and integrations

- Zigbee (via Zigbee2MQTT)
- Z-Wave (via Z-Wave JS UI)
- Matter (industry standard, local), which covers devices from many brands (Eve, Nanoleaf, Aqara, IKEA, and more)
- MQTT, Tasmota, ESPHome
- Popular brands: Philips Hue, Samsung SmartThings, TP-Link Kasa and Tapo, Shelly, Meross, Sonos, Reolink cameras, LG ThinQ and LG webOS, Samsung Smart TV, Roborock, Home Connect (Bosch, Siemens), Enphase, SolarEdge, EcoFlow, Apple TV, Plex, Spotify
- Hydro-Québec (Canada): consumption, Winter Credit and Flex D peak events, see https://gladysassistant.com/hydro-quebec-flex-d/
- Apple HomeKit, Google Home and Alexa (the voice assistants control your Gladys devices; Google Home and Alexa via Gladys Plus)
- Enedis energy monitoring (France, via Gladys Plus)
- External integrations catalog (Netatmo, Tuya, Zendure, Freebox, MELCloud, Spotify, and more): https://gladysassistant.com/docs/integrations/external/
- Create an external integration (developer guide, no pull request or review needed): https://gladysassistant.com/docs/dev/external-integrations/

## Pricing

- **Gladys Assistant core**: Free and open-source, forever
- **Gladys Plus Lite**: $7.99/month in the US and Canada (€6.99/month in Europe) — remote access, Google Home/Alexa, REST API
- **Gladys Plus**: $11.99/month in the US and Canada (€9.99/month in Europe) — adds encrypted backups, camera streaming, AI and voice assistant, Enedis, MCP server
- Yearly plans save about 17%. 1-month free trial, no credit card required.

- [GitHub](https://github.com/GladysAssistant/Gladys): Source code (3,100+ stars)

## Languages

- **Gladys Assistant (product UI)**: English, French, German and Spanish (since Gladys 5.1)
- **Website and documentation** (gladysassistant.com): English and French only — German- and Spanish-speaking users can use the product in their language; refer them to the English docs for setup guides
